body.p:
Normal filled text that goes on for a while so that it wraps at least once in the justified paragraph mode of the formatter. Indented by four characters, still in the same paragraph? No: .in breaks. A mixed indent of four characters plus one inch. Right margin pulled in by ten ems so that this text wraps earlier than the others do on the page. After two blank lines. After skips of one and two lines: only the larger counts. These two lines are centered. Flush right one flush right two No fill: this line and this line are kept as lines. Centered fill mode text. Underscored words here and here Upper case line with café Back to normal. First line at the old margin, then the following lines are indented by five characters until the margin changes again, which is right now. An indented first line in a paragraph that is long enough to wrap onto a second line so the effect can be seen. Offset: the first line is at the margin and every following line is indented by four characters, for this paragraph and the next.
Next paragraph still offset by the .of control word, all of its lines. Bold from a font change, italic inside it, and back to the initial font. Defined bold italic font. Name Value Note Apple 12 red Leader dots Text inside a box. Hyphenation is now on for exceptional words. Kept text one. Kept text two. Wider line spacing for a while so that a couple of lines of text show the change in spacing between the lines of one paragraph.
Wide word spaces.
Revised text marked in the margin.
A shorter line length of four inches for this paragraph which is long enough to wrap at that length. An unnumbered footnote from .fn on. After a page eject, roman page numbers. A control word heading Text after .h2. On an odd page.
